**Indikator 4a1** is a specific clinical quality indicator used in Denmark to measure the proportion of patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation who have a clinical indication for [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] and actually receive this treatment one year after their index date. The national standard for this indicator is set at ≥ 90% [^src1].

This metric is a core component of the annual quality monitoring conducted by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), as detailed in the 2024 'Atrieflimren i Danmark' (AFDK) report. It specifically tracks 1-year treatment coverage—alongside Indikator 4a2, which tracks 2-year coverage—to evaluate adherence to national guidelines. By providing quantitative results at the national, regional, and local health cluster levels, the indicator supports a hierarchical quality improvement strategy that helps healthcare providers identify strengths and weaknesses in their clinical practice. 

For the 2022/23 measurement period, which ran from July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023, the national average for [[danmark|Danmark]] was 89.1% (95% CI: 88.5–89.7), falling just short of the 90% target [^src1]. Performance varied across different geographies. [[region-nordjylland|Nordjylland]] successfully met the standard, achieving a coverage rate of 92.1% (95% CI: 90.4–93.6) [^src1]. Conversely, [[region-midtjylland|Midtjylland]] narrowly missed the benchmark with a rate of 89.2% (95% CI: 87.9–90.4) [^src1]. At the local level, [[sundhedsklyngen-nykoebing-f|Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F]] recorded the lowest proportion for the indicator at 85.1% (95% CI: 81.2–88.4) [^src1].
